Definition: of Hebrew origin (H2396); Ezekias (i.e. Hezekeiah), an Israelite:--Ezekias.
BiblicalUsage: Ezekias is the Greek form of Hezekiah, and it appears in Matthew's genealogy: Achaz begat Ezekias in Matthew 1:9, and Ezekias begat Manasses in Matthew 1:10. The name stands in the line of kings that leads to Jesus, between Ahaz and Manasseh. Matthew spells it the Greek way because he is writing the family line for a Greek-speaking world.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Matthew put Hezekiah in this list on purpose, not as filler. A reforming king who trusted God against Assyria belongs in the ancestry of the Messiah, and his name reminds me that God works through real kings with real failures around them.
